correctness.rationale: The derivation D_f=f(t)d/dt exists for arbitrary f when N even and requires f_0=0 when odd. Characteristic 2 makes D_f^2 a derivation with D_f^2(t)=ff' mod t^N. If the leading exponent s is odd, square-zero is equivalent to 2s-1>=N; for even s=2j with 4j<N, invertibility of the leading unit reduces to the stated vanishing of odd coefficients in a finite interval. The resulting linear-space family contains exactly all extension-field points; consecutive coordinate support differences give codimension-one intersections, while nonconsecutive ones lie within the predecessor intersection. Therefore the union is reduced support with c noncontained irreducible components and the point formula. The t coefficient of ff' is f_1^2, while the homogeneous quadratic ideal cannot contain nonzero linear f_1, proving a nonzero nilpotent; tangent at zero sees only the optional linear constraint. Independently enumerated every F2 coefficient vector for N=2..12, checked square-zero, union membership and predicted point counts.
